newsitem.title: CONGO: Mandela reaches ship venue of Zaire peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mandela reaches ship venue of Zaire peace talks.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela stepped on board a naval ship in a Congolese port on Friday, ready to host the first direct peace talks between Zaire's warring leaders.
Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko was due to have boarded the South African ship Outeniqua with Mandela but remained initially in the port of Pointe Noire to which he had flown earlier.

His arch foe Laurent Kabila, whose rebels have taken around three-quarters of Zaire in a rebellion since October, was in the Angolan capital Luanda and believed to be on his way to join the ship which was to head out into international waters.
Mandela said he was optimistic despite delays in starting the talks in a special air-conditioned but windowless container on the deck of the grey former ice-breaker.

"We are dealing with two outstanding leaders who are conscious of the importance of an amicable settlement which will satisfy both of them as well as the people of Zaire," Mandela told reporters on the ship.

"I am confident the two leaders realise the importance of a peaceful settlement," he said, adding: "I know few leaders who have made military gains and nevertheless been committed to peace as Mr Kabila has."
The sea off the Congolese coast was calm despite earlier heavy rains.
